prize_categories.title: Sperry Tech — The GridLock Challenge
prize_categories.description:
Power grid companies ("utilities") each plan future construction projects years in advance. Neighboring utilities in different states often plan this work without much visibility into what the other is doing nearby.
Build a tool that compares at least two utilities' public future construction plans and flags where their planned work overlaps, either because the projects are physically close to each other or because they're scheduled around the same time.
The goal is to help utilities coordinate nearby projects so they can potentially share labor, equipment, and other critical resources.

prize_categories.title: Assurant — Take Control of AI
prize_categories.description:
AI is reshaping daily life, but most users don't know what data they're sharing, what they're spending, or whether they've picked the right tool.
Build something that gives people real control through privacy protection, spending visibility, or confident tool selection.
The broader question is: How do we make sure people in a connected world use AI mindfully?

prize_categories.title: Waymo — The Waymo Mobility Challenge
prize_categories.description:
Create a hack that improves transportation using publicly available data.
Possible approaches include APIs for directions, 360-degree street view, aerial view, elevation data, time zones, and other public data.
Example ideas include an app helping students carpool to campus or a social network for sharing and reviewing cafes for studying.
Publicly available data such as Google Maps data may be used.

prize_categories.title: Microsoft — What's Missing?
prize_categories.description:
Pick something that feels unnecessarily difficult, inaccessible, outdated, or simply missing, and build an AI-powered experience that makes it better.
The goal is to use AI as part of the experience rather than making AI the entire experience.
Build something that helps a person do something they couldn't easily do before and demonstrate the difference it makes.

Requirements: The core experience cannot be a chatbot or depend on a chat window. The demo should show someone accomplishing a real task, making something, discovering something, testing something, or improving something, rather than simply asking AI for an answer.

prize_categories.title: Blackstone — Reimagining the Investor Experience
prize_categories.description:
Build a product that reimagines how investors understand their current investments and research new opportunities.
Potential solutions may help users analyze existing portfolios, compare investment opportunities, discover trends and risks, summarize complex information, visualize performance, or ask questions in natural language.
Publicly available financial or economic data may be used, and any technology stack may be chosen.
Solutions should make financial information more accessible, actionable, and engaging.

prize_categories.title: State Farm — Auto Insurance Challenge
prize_categories.description:
Create a hack that makes auto insurance simpler and more helpful for students and helps reduce everyday risks such as theft, fire, or accidents where students live, study, or travel.
Features could include helpful tools, gamified experiences, or education.

prize_categories.title: INIT National — Building Together
prize_categories.description:
Build technology that helps student builders collaborate to create great projects together.
Explore challenges students face when working together beyond a short hackathon, whether over weeks or months and whether working in-person or remotely.
Solutions may help students find teammates, learn from one another, share knowledge, ask for help, receive mentorship, overcome roadblocks, and stay engaged.
The solution should not only manage work. It should help people build relationships, contribute at different skill levels, and become better builders together.

prize_categories.title: MLH × ElevenLabs — Best Use of ElevenLabs
prize_categories.description:
Deploy natural, human-sounding audio with ElevenLabs.
Projects may create realistic, dynamic, and emotionally expressive voices for experiences such as interactive AI companions, narrated stories, and voice-enabled applications.
Integrate fully autonomous audio experiences into the hack using ElevenLabs.

prize_categories.title: MLH × Google Cloud — Best Use of Gemini API
prize_categories.description:
Use the Google Gemini API to build an AI-powered hackathon project.
Examples given include understanding language to provide personalized advice, analyzing and summarizing complex research information, and generating creative content such as code, scripts, and music.

Requirements: Use the Gemini API in the hackathon project.

prize_categories.title: MLH × Solana — Best Use of Solana
prize_categories.description:
Build applications using Solana's fast execution and near-zero transaction costs.
Suggested directions include games, social apps, or consumer products using instant high-frequency transactions; sophisticated trading, lending, or decentralized exchanges; and prototypes involving supply chain, identity, or payments at large real-world scale.

prize_categories.title: MLH × Tiger Data — Best Use of Tiger Data
prize_categories.description:
Use Tiger Data's PostgreSQL-based platform for high-performance applications involving real-time data, time-series metrics, and complex analytics.
Highlighted capabilities include standard SQL over large datasets, storing relational profiles alongside high-frequency metric streams, real-time dashboards using Continuous Aggregates, and data compression.
Example projects include real-time IoT monitoring, AI-driven analytics dashboards, and financial prediction engines.

prize_categories.title: MLH × DigitalOcean — Best Use of DigitalOcean
prize_categories.description:
Build, deploy, and scale a project using DigitalOcean.
Relevant services mentioned include Droplets, Managed Databases, App Platform, and DigitalOcean Gradient AI for building, training, deploying, and serving machine-learning models.

prize_categories.title: MLH × Snowflake — Best Use of Snowflake API
prize_categories.description:
Use Snowflake APIs to add AI capabilities to an application.
Suggested approaches include customized applications, RAG-powered chatbots, or embedding AI-powered functionality using Snowflake's APIs.
The challenge information also mentions a student 120-day Snowflake trial and an example repository demonstrating the Snowflake REST API.

prize_categories.title: MLH × MongoDB — Best Use of MongoDB Atlas
prize_categories.description:
Build a hack using MongoDB Atlas.
MongoDB Atlas provides cloud database services and related functionality, with student resources and MongoDB University resources available.

prize_categories.title: MLH × GoDaddy Registry — Best Domain Name from GoDaddy Registry
prize_categories.description: Register and use a domain name with GoDaddy Registry as part of the hack.
